Definition: from G3474; to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton:--become fool, make foolish, lose savour.
BiblicalUsage: Moraino means to become insipid, to lose savour. Salt that has lost its savour is good for nothing but to be cast out, and Paul says God has made foolish the wisdom of this world, while men professing themselves wise became fools.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word cuts both ways. Salt can go flat, and wisdom can go foolish, and in both cases the loss is the loss of what the thing was for.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
